title: 2018 AMC 8 Problem 21
statement: How many positive three-digit integers have a remainder of \(2\) when divided by \(6,\) a remainder of \(5\) when divided by \(9,\) and a remainder of \(7\) when divided by \(11?\)

solutions.text:
Each required remainder is \(4\) less than its divisor, so \(x+4\) must be divisible by \(6,9,\) and \(11\). Hence \(x+4\) is a multiple of \(\operatorname{lcm}(6,9,11)=198.\)

For a three-digit \(x\), we have \(104\le x+4\le1003\). The multiples of \(198\) in this interval are \(198,396,594,792,990\), giving \(5\) possible integers.

Thus, E is the correct answer.
hints: Each remainder condition says the number is \(4\) less than a multiple of the divisor.
Count three-digit numbers of the form \(198k-4\).
